obligations.description: Replace the written file `.acceptance/next-instruction.md` with the `acceptance recommendation --criterion <id> [--format json|text]` command surface for retrieving a criterion's recommendation on demand, defaulting to JSON.
obligations.evidence_rationale: PARTLY REAL (judgement.md, run 1). A compound umbrella obligation whose constituents the other eleven cover individually — a #144-shaped decomposition artifact, so the mapper reasonably preferred the specific obligations. But its 'defaulting to JSON' clause appears in no other obligation and was tested only implicitly, by a test that happened to json.loads the output. Only that clause is the real finding.

obligations.description: Keep the recommendation retrieval command surface fixed to the specified command name and arguments in the specification.
obligations.evidence_rationale: REAL GAP (judgement.md, run 1). #167 fixed the command surface up front precisely so the spec could name it, and nothing pinned the spec string to the parser — the drift this task exists to prevent. Its two mapped tests are unrelated: mapping noise on top of a genuine gap.

obligations.description: Ensure recommendation retrieval performs no speculative writes so nothing can go stale.
obligations.evidence_rationale: UNEARNED STRONG (corpus table; corrected by run 3). Run 1 issued strongly supported on evidence that did not earn it. Run 3 established the real gap: no test snapshots the repo around `recommendation` itself.

obligations.description: Return a recommendation from stored review state on demand without re-running the review.
obligations.evidence_rationale: UNEARNED STRONG (corpus table; corrected by run 2). Run 2 established the real gap: nothing distinguished 'read stored state' from 'recomputed and happened to agree', and nothing proved the named revision was read.

obligations.description: Keep the recommendation's structured fields as discrete keys with their prose values intact.
obligations.evidence_rationale: Rated strongly supported by this run, and its judgement.md does not dispute it. Recorded as the run's reading rather than as a separately established fact.

obligations.description: Make the review's own output tell a reader how to obtain the recommendation detail.
obligations.evidence_rationale: Rated strongly supported by this run, and its judgement.md does not dispute it. Recorded as the run's reading rather than as a separately established fact.

obligations.description: Remove any pre-existing `.acceptance/next-instruction.md` left by an earlier version and report that it was removed.
obligations.evidence_rationale: UNEARNED STRONG (corpus table; corrected by run 3). Runs 1 and 2 both rated this strongly supported while `--json` mode deleted a file in the user's repo and printed nothing.

obligations.description: Leave the review's own output as the only statement of status when starting from a repo that already contains `.acceptance/next-instruction.md`.
obligations.evidence_rationale: Rated strongly supported by this run, and its judgement.md does not dispute it. Recorded as the run's reading rather than as a separately established fact.

obligations.description: Return an empty result when a criterion has no recommendation.
obligations.evidence_rationale: Rated strongly supported by this run, and its judgement.md does not dispute it. Recorded as the run's reading rather than as a separately established fact.

obligations.description: Default retrieval to the most recently stored review when the caller does not name one.
obligations.evidence_rationale: UNEARNED STRONG, stated outright in run 1's own retrospective: 'run 1's STRONG here was a false negative: the rating was wrong, not merely unstable.' Its only test stored a single review, so it could not distinguish 'the newest' from 'the only one' — a test that did not verify its own name.

obligations.description: Produce byte-identical output for repeated retrievals over unchanged review state.
obligations.evidence_rationale: Rated strongly supported by this run, and its judgement.md does not dispute it. Recorded as the run's reading rather than as a separately established fact.

obligations.description: Keep the specification from describing the recommendation as a written file.
obligations.evidence_rationale: UNEARNED STRONG (corpus table; corrected by run 3). The spec still described the recommendation as surfacing in a Markdown file; the test asserted only that one filename was absent.
